propositions: Six bridge-related verbs (reconcile, jira-onboard, bridge-probe, bridge-status, bridge-fsck, purge-bridge) leak internal mechanics and couple rebar core to GitHub Actions; two verbs are dead (bridge-status producer never existed, purge-bridge has no callers).

The --mode flag fuses two orthogonal concepts (change scope and execution eligibility) making the surface unexplainable without internals; splitting into --max-changes and pause/resume with plain-language docs is required.
rebar core shells out to gh binary for fsck safety precondition, violating portability and silencing repair guards for non-GitHub environments; this dependency must be eliminated.

Approximately 185 lines of logic live in GHA workflow including a 106-line CAS push loop that reimplements and has diverged from _store/push.py in both directions; duplication and divergence must be resolved.

The canonical bridge surface (setup, check-access, fsck, status, preview, sync, pause, resume) must be portable across local, GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab, and bare environments with verified identical behavior and no vendor-specific reads or required external binaries.

Every existing in-repo workflow, environment config, script, test, and documented invocation must migrate to the new primary vocabulary in the same shippable change; legacy entrypoints (reconcile, bridge-status) remain functional with old contracts during the migration.
